mcqs.question: Which of the following sentences uses a subordinate clause incorrectly?

options.A: Although she was tired, she finished her homework.
options.B: She finished her homework although she was tired.
options.C: She was tired because she finished her homework.
options.D: Because she was tired, she finished her homework.

mcqs.answer: She was tired because she finished her homework.
mcqs.explanation: Option C reverses the logical relationship: the reason (being tired) should cause the action (finishing homework), not the other way round. The correct causal clause would be "She finished her homework because she was tired". Options A, B and D correctly place subordinate clauses.

mcqs.question: Select the correct passive‑voice transformation of the sentence: "The committee will approve the proposal tomorrow."

options.A: The proposal will be approved by the committee tomorrow.
options.B: The proposal will approve the committee tomorrow.
options.C: The committee will be approved by the proposal tomorrow.
options.D: Tomorrow, the proposal will approve the committee.

mcqs.answer: The proposal will be approved by the committee tomorrow.
mcqs.explanation: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject, the verb takes the appropriate form of "be" plus past participle, and the original subject is introduced by "by". Option A follows this pattern. Options B, C and D misuse the verb and do not form a proper passive construction.

mcqs.question: Which sentence correctly changes the direct speech "He said, 'I will finish the assignment by Friday.'" into indirect speech?

options.A: He said that he will finish the assignment by Friday.
options.B: He said that he would finish the assignment by Friday.
options.C: He said that I will finish the assignment by Friday.
options.D: He said that he had finished the assignment by Friday.

mcqs.answer: He said that he would finish the assignment by Friday.
mcqs.explanation: When converting present‑future direct speech to indirect speech, the verb shifts back one tense: "will" becomes "would". Option B reflects this shift correctly. Option A keeps the original tense, C changes the pronoun, and D changes the meaning to past perfect.

mcqs.question: In the sentence "Neither of the students have completed their project," which grammatical error is present?
mcqs.explanation: "Neither" is singular, so the verb must be singular: "Neither of the students has completed their project." Therefore the error is a subject‑verb agreement mistake. The other options do not describe the problem in this sentence.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an adverb?

options.A: A word that describes a noun.
options.C: A word that modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.

mcqs.answer: A word that modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
mcqs.explanation: An adverb provides information about how, when, where, how much, or to what extent an action or quality occurs, thus modifying verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. Options A, B, and D describe nouns, verbs, and conjunctions respectively.

mcqs.question: Identify the sentence that uses pronouns correctly.

options.A: Him and I went to the market.
options.B: He and I went to the market.
options.C: Me and him went to the market.
options.D: I and he went to the market.

mcqs.answer: He and I went to the market.
mcqs.explanation: Subject pronouns "he" and "I" are required in the subject position. Option B follows this rule. Options A and C use object pronouns in the subject position, and while option D uses correct pronouns, the conventional order is "He and I," making B the best choice.

mcqs.question: Which sentence uses an adverb correctly?
mcqs.explanation: The adverb "beautifully" modifies the verb "sings" and describes how she sings. Option A incorrectly uses the adjective "beautiful" after a verb. Option C misplaces the adverb before a noun, and option D uses the adjective correctly but does not test adverb usage.

mcqs.question: Choose the sentence that uses an auxiliary verb correctly to express a future intention.

options.A: I will going to the party tonight.
options.B: I am going to the party tonight.
options.C: I will go to the party tonight.
options.D: I go to the party tonight.

mcqs.answer: I will go to the party tonight.
mcqs.explanation: The auxiliary "will" + base form of the main verb "go" correctly expresses a future intention. Option A misplaces the gerund, B uses present progressive (present intention), and D is simple present, which does not convey future intention.
